subject: NimblePay integration: auth, SDK bootstrap, and routing — proposed action plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.b@nimblepay.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi.p@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimblePay integration: auth, SDK bootstrap, and routing — proposed action plan

Hi Laura / Ravi —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the PoC and security review: 

1) Goals from our side:
- Validate end-to-end integration for payments context enrichment (embeddings + reranker) with a Redwood-hosted inference endpoint.
- Confirm secure auth model that meets NimblePay SOC2 requirements and allows programmatic rotation.
- Demonstrate low-latency routing (region-aware) and structured output for payment reconciliation tool-calls.

2) Key constraints you mentioned:
- Must use customer-managed service accounts for server-to-server calls (no long-lived static API keys in CI).
- All keys stored in your KMS (AWS KMS) with automatic rotation policies.
- Audit logs required for all token exchanges and model invocations.

3) Options we recommend for the PoC (we can pick one together):
A) Service-account JWT flow (recommended): Redwood accepts short-lived signed JWTs from NimblePay service accounts; we mint short-term tokens scoped to the model + route. Supports rotation and auditable token exchange.
B) OAuth 2.0 with client_credentials (acceptable): centrally-managed client_id/secret via your vault; Redwood issues temporary session tokens and logs token use.
C) Scoped API keys (expiring): for quick start only, with automated rotation helpers — not preferred for production.

4) Technical asks from our side for the PoC:
- Provide a service account key or a signed-JWT endpoint (we can support both).
- Example sequences for your KMS rotation policy and any existing token broker you use.
- A short list of 3 sample prompts and two reranker datasets we can run to baseline latency/cost.

5) Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (next week): security sync (NimblePay security + Redwood infra) to confirm JWT/OAuth approach.
- Week 1–2: SDK bootstrap + auth handshake (we’ll provide a reference Node/Python flow).
- Week 3: run latency & quality benchmarks on your sample traffic; demo results and next steps.

Attachments: nimblepay-sso-requirements.pdf (you shared), redwood-poc-scope.xlsx (draft).

Next step: Can we lock a 30-min security sync on Tue/Wed next week? I’ll loop in Aditya from our infra/security team and Marissa for the integration plan.

Best,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.b@nimblepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: NimblePay Security <security@nimblepay.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi.p@nimblepay.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimblePay integration: auth, SDK bootstrap, and routing — proposed action plan

Ben —

Thanks for the thorough recap. Quick responses inline: 

> Service-account JWT flow (recommended)
This aligns best with our internal policies. We operate short-lived signed JWTs issued by our identity broker (runs in our VPC). We can:
- Provide a signed-JWT endpoint for Redwood to validate (preferred), or
- Provide a service account private key (PKCS8) if that’s necessary for initial PoC.

> Audit logs required for all token exchanges and model invocations
We’ll need to see the token exchange logs from Redwood (request id, timestamp, model id, route). Can you confirm the format and retention defaults?

> KMS + rotation
We store keys in AWS KMS; rotation is every 90 days. We do not allow exported private keys for production.

We’re happy to do the security sync. Tue 25 May, 11:00am PT works on our side.

Attached: nimblepay-sso-requirements.pdf (high-level SSO & token rules).

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Product Engineering
NimblePay
laura.b@nimblepay.com

Subject: Re: NimblePay integration: auth, SDK bootstrap, and routing — proposed action plan

Laura / security team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and for confirming Tue 25 May 11:00am PT for the security sync. A few clarifying points so the call is productive: 

- Logs & retention: Redwood can provide structured invocation logs (JSON lines) with fields: request_id, timestamp, requester_identity (service-account-id), model_id, route, input_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, latency_ms. Default retention for the hosted PoC will be 90 days; we can extend per contract.

- Signed-JWT validation: We support both JWKS endpoint validation (preferable) and static public key upload. If you can host a JWKS endpoint for the service account keys that will avoid key export.

- Token lifecycle: For the PoC we can accept a short-lived JWT from your broker and exchange it for a Redwood session token with TTL 15 minutes. All exchanges will be logged and surface in the Console audit trail.

- SDK bootstrap: Marissa will follow up with a minimal Node example that demonstrates:
  * getting a signed JWT from your broker (mocked in example),
  * exchanging for a Redwood session token,
  * hitting the /v1/chat/stream endpoint with structured tool-calls, and
  * showing embedding + reranker wiring.

Actions before Tue:
- Laura / security: send JWKS URL or upload key thumbprints we can validate.
- NimblePay: confirm whether private key export is allowed for PoC (temporary) or not.
- Redwood: Marissa will post the PoC scaffold to the Drive link and Aditya will join Tue’s call.

Ben

--

- Marissa, please finalize the PoC scaffold (Node + Python) demonstrating the JWT->session token flow, plus a tiny example of structured output for a reconciliation tool-call and embeddings->reranker usage. Put artifacts in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cNimblepay-PoC

I’ll join Tue’s call and handle the commercial/next-step items.

Ben
